routes.description: Establish that action necessarily expresses a highest-order value structure, that the West's operative structure is substantially inherited through religious narratives and institutions, and that this inheritance supplies indispensable resources for morality, meaning, suffering, and social coordination.
routes.successCriteria: Show that secular professions and practices do not constitute a self-sufficient replacement because coherent conduct, durable ethics, and tragedy-sustaining meaning continue to depend on functions performed by God, religious stories, or religiously inherited values.

motionBridge.description: Connect the unavoidable requirements of coherent action, moral order, and meaning under suffering to God, religious narrative, or inherited religious values.

centralBridges.description: Establish that conduct embodies a hierarchy of values whose highest commitment performs the functional role attributed to God.
Explain why secular morality and institutions remain dependent on inherited commitments such as individual sovereignty and truthful speech.
Show why religious narratives provide meaning capable of organizing action through unavoidable tragedy and human malevolence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Ground religious archetypes and ethical patterns in culturally and biologically deep structures of adaptive conduct.
Account for the vacuum and destabilizing substitutes that may follow removal of inherited religious foundations.

routes.description: Establish that biological and memetic evolution can explain religion, morality, and higher meanings without divine grounding, while secular reflection, contemplative practice, and ordinary social life can sustain motivation, gratitude, ethical conduct, and acceptance of suffering.
routes.successCriteria: Provide a sufficient secular account of meaning and morality, distinguish religious usefulness from religious necessity or divine truth, and show that functioning persons and societies can relinquish God without the predicted collapse into nihilism or disorder.

motionBridge.description: Demonstrate that humans can make sense of action, morality, suffering, and meaning through secular evolutionary, cultural, and experiential resources.

centralBridges.description: Explain religious persistence and higher meaning through distinct biological and cultural replication processes without requiring divine causation.
Show how secular reflection, meditation, evolved motivation, and social life can support gratitude, ethical conduct, and purposeful action.
Use secular persons and societies as counterexamples to claims that abandoning God necessarily produces moral or social collapse.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate the practical wisdom or social benefits of religious traditions from claims of divine causation, guilt, or necessity.
Require an explanation of prosocial atheist conduct that does not redefine all moral behavior as implicitly religious.

sections.title: Belief, conduct, and the functional meaning of God
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether every coherent value hierarchy is properly understood as religious and whether moral atheist conduct confirms that thesis or supplies a secular counterexample.

sections.title: Secular ethics, stable societies, and religious inheritance
sections.rationale: The necessity claim turns substantially on whether morality and stable institutions can stand independently or remain downstream of inherited religious commitments and vulnerable when those foundations recede.

sections.title: Evolutionary archetypes, memes, and religious persistence
sections.rationale: Competing biological and cultural explanations bear on whether religious patterns encode indispensable realities of successful conduct or persist as historically contingent, independently copied complexes.

sections.title: Religious and secular responses to tragedy and ultimate meaning
sections.rationale: Because the motion expressly concerns suffering and life's meaning, this section tests whether religious stories uniquely sustain action through tragedy or whether acceptance of cosmic pointlessness remains compatible with positive living.

sections.title: Secular gratitude and the construction of higher meaning
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether gratitude and coordinated higher-order meaning require an implicit divine object or can emerge through contemplative practice, evolved needs, and memetic cultural construction.
